en: I have a devout faith in God
note: Verb split into #561 so each row keeps its own Japanese part

en: that I cannot cast aside.
Now I have come to be loved by everyone
but even so, the depths of my heart always
return to that grave sin.
That is also the punishment that torments me.
The place you will return to
note: The verb for 'return' rendered consistently as 'return' (Ramon's own heart 'returns' to his sin in #564/#586, so the contrast with this listener is kept)

en: is not, however, steeped in sin.
You should be able to return.
Such a thing,
I have already cast away.
I have no place to return to.
I see.
Then I shall say no more.
May God's blessing be upon you.
Welcome to our church.
This is a place of prayer to God.
Have you come to offer prayers again?
note: Message 25437 places this before #541 ('I am Ramon, the priest.'): read literally, 'Have you come to pray again? I am Ramon.' - order kept as listed

en: Reflected in your eyes is a deep abyss,
and within it I glimpse light and darkness.
But you,
you still seem to have a choice of paths.
note: Source: 'seems to still have a means of choosing a path'; compressed to fit 3 lines

en: May you not choose the path I chose...
note: Object of the verb is 'the same path as mine'; written as 'the path I chose' (his sin)

en: Now I have come to be loved by everyone,
and they say my sin has been purified,
yet even so, the depths of my heart
always return to that grave sin.
And that, too,
is the punishment that torments me.
You will learn to waver and to suffer.
In time you'll also know the path of despair.
note: The 'yield/surrender' nuance dropped for fit: 'surrender to despair' made the 3-line message overflow

en: But you must not choose it.
Even if you walk a path that defies God,
you are able to return, after all.
note: Also used in msg 25531 where the row reads the same; 'after all' carries the explanatory ending

en: As long as you do not cast away that heart...
Father.
You told me I have a place to return to.
note: Referent of 'place to return to' = the 'place to return to' Ramon promised (#566-568)

en: So you told me to believe, for now...
note: Imperative = 'you told me to'; the subject is Ramon's command (Christopher quoting him)

en: That is why I will do this, if you will allow it...
note: Referent of 'this' unknown (action in the following scene), kept vague as in the source

en: I have no other way left, as I am now...
Believing that this is right...
, my master, only to you
note: The name + honorific cannot be moved before the name, so 'my master' follows the inserted name; 'only to you' carries the 'alone'

en: will I devote myself
note: Polite verb form, deferential tone for a gruff man; trailing ... is #66

en: Hmm,
Lately my body just won't do what I tell it.
Morning. I'm Halk the blacksmith.
And who are you?
I am
note: With #8/#13 '.' gives 'I am Name.' (Daedalus 74348, Sati 82591 also fine)

en: I see.
Nice to meet you.
Morning.
Morning,
note: Name + '.' via #13

en: Heading to my workshop. Want to come watch again?
note: 'Morning, Name.' is in the previous fragment, so this row is shortened to fit in 3 lines

en: Hey. I'm Halk the blacksmith.
I'm on my way home.
Hey,
Hey,
note: Shared with Katusa (#143 '.'), Southwark (#13 '.'): 'Hey, Name.' as agreed in followups (#201)

en: Tell me if you're ever in trouble.
I've taken a liking to you, you know.
I'm Halk the blacksmith. And you?
This is my house.
I live here with my two daughters.
I'm Halk the blacksmith.
Say, those things I've made,
note: Shares #624 with msg 30101 whose #661 (other slice) must end so that 'have you ever seen them?' reads: e.g. 'Say, those iron tools I've made,'

en: have you ever seen them?
Take a look.
You'll see just how skilled a smith
note: Shares #627 with msg 30101 whose #662 (other slice) must end '...how skilled a smith' so that 'I am, I reckon.' completes it

en: I am, I reckon.
Have you seen the things I make?
Well, you don't get much chance to see them.
If there's a horse around, you could just flip it over
note: Flipping the horse over = look at the horseshoes (cf. #645 'horseshoes'); the joke kept literal

en: and take a look. That'd do it.
. Glad you came.
note: Follows 'Hey, Name' (#616 + name)

en: Make yourself at home.
Come again.
Hm? And who are you?
Got some business with Halk's workshop here?
note: Halk refers to himself in third person

en: No, I am only looking.
I see, look all you like.
Just don't get too close.
